provenanceNote: Formerly id "se-coordination-number-day-61-resolves-to-first". That name claimed the fixture proved day 61 resolves to the 1st, but reshaping 20190101-2391's day (01→61) invalidates the original check digit, so this never reaches date resolution at all — it only ever asserted checksum-mismatch. Renamed to describe what it actually tests; the real day-61-resolves-to-first behaviour is now proven separately by se-coordination-number-day-61-parses-to-first, using an official Skatteverket number. See docs/open-threads.md and PROVENANCE.md for the incident.

Formerly id "se-coordination-number-day-91-resolves-to-thirty-first". Same issue as se-coordination-number-invalid-checksum-day-61: reshaping the day (31→91) invalidates the checksum before date resolution is ever reached, so this only ever asserted checksum-mismatch. The real day-91-resolves-to-thirty-first behaviour is now proven separately by se-coordination-number-day-91-parses-to-thirty-first, using an official Skatteverket number.

Added alongside the pre-existing se-coordination-number-scheme-not-allowed (which uses a constructed, invalid-checksum input). This one proves the allowCoordinationNumber:false gate blocks a genuinely valid, official coordination number, not only a reshaped-invalid one.
